sheets.title: The category portfolio
sheets.headline:
The largest spend is not always
the strongest evidence.

blocks.text: All six modelled categories, plotted against the completed ERA work behind each one. Two advance first. None of the others leaves the portfolio.

columns.text: Why these two

Operating Supply leads because the filing position is distinctive — 98th percentile of 2,573 peer filers — and the dollar question is large. Uniforms follows because the filing names the relationship and ERA has deeper completed-work evidence.
Why the rest stay
Every other category remains in the portfolio. Fleet carries the fewest completed engagements of the six, which is a reason to validate it with your data rather than to model it harder.

columns.text: Why the ranges are wide
Commercial structure, specifications, service levels, contract age and operating constraints differ. That is precisely why a benchmark alone is not enough.
What ERA adds
A category specialist builds the baseline, validates the commercial position, develops options, supports implementation and measures the verified result.

sheets.title: Two places to begin
sheets.headline:
Two categories, two different questions,
two different specialists.

columns.text: Operating Supply · $37.97M
The question: how much is resale inventory and how much is supply consumed in the operation?
Why first: 98th percentile of 2,573 peers; 69 completed ERA engagements; the dollar question is material.
ERA would: separate the spend, build the supplier-item-location baseline, normalize requirements, test the commercial structure and implement the approved result.
Completed-work median: $8.09M against the filed figure. Not an estimate of recovery here.
Uniforms, Workwear and Linens · $1.52M
The question: was the agreement re-marketed or quietly renewed, and what does the full commercial structure contain?
Why second: the filing names the relationship; 109 completed engagements provide deeper category evidence.
ERA would: read the agreement, reconcile invoice reality, validate service requirements, compare the complete structure and support the approved action.
Completed-work median: $427K against the filed figure. Not an estimate of recovery here.

sheets.title: Beyond the filing
sheets.headline:
The filing is a map of where to start.
Your operating data reveals the full territory.

blocks.text: A Form 990 reports selected lines for tax disclosure, not for category management. It rarely separates waste, telecom, packaging, payment processing, utilities, maintenance, office supply and many other recurring operating costs. ERA works across 55 categories, but only Goodwill's internal data can establish which are applicable and worth testing.

blocks.text: In the conversation. We will test the two assumptions that most affect the current analysis: how much of the $37.97M supply line is resale inventory, and when the named service arrangements were last tested.

columns.text: If the questions hold
We build a no-cost category baseline from your data, identify the applicable portfolio and show which arrangements should remain and which merit action.
If the questions do not hold
We say so. Independent validation is a useful result, and there is no fee.
If verified value exists
You decide what to pursue. ERA supports implementation and is paid only from recovery after you receive it.
